concepts.title: Business Transactions, Source Documents and Vouchers
concepts.definition: Every business transaction is evidenced by a source document such as a cash memo, invoice, cheque or pay-in-slip, and the accountant prepares an accounting voucher on its basis before the transaction is recorded in the books.
concepts.key_idea: Source documents provide the evidence for the entry, and vouchers classify the transaction as debit or credit voucher with a narration.

concepts.title: The Accounting Equation
concepts.definition: The accounting equation states that assets are equal to capital plus liabilities, so every transaction keeps the two sides equal and capital can always be recovered as assets minus liabilities.
concepts.key_idea: Each transaction changes at least two elements of the equation, but the equality of total assets and total claims never breaks.

solution_steps.explain: Deduct liabilities from total assets to obtain the capital claim
Deduct capital from total assets to obtain the outsiders claim

concepts.title: Rules of Debit and Credit for Accounts
concepts.definition: Under the modern approach, increases in assets and expenses are debited while decreases are credited; increases in capital, liabilities and incomes are credited while decreases are debited, keeping total debits equal to total credits.
concepts.key_idea: Applying the rules to the affected accounts decides which account is debited and which is credited for any transaction.

solution_steps.explain: Place each affected account under asset, liability, capital, income or expense.
Decide debit or credit from the direction of change in each account.
Confirm the total debit amount equals the total credit amount.

concepts.title: Journal, Narration and Compound Entries
concepts.definition: The journal is the book of original entry where transactions are first recorded chronologically with a narration; a compound entry records several debits or credits in one entry, and the process is called journalising.
concepts.key_idea: The journal entry shows date, accounts, amounts, folio and narration, forming the base for posting into the ledger.

solution_steps.explain: Identify the accounts affected and the nature of each.

concepts.title: Trade Discount and Net Invoice Price
concepts.definition: When a trade discount is allowed on the list price of goods, the invoice is prepared at the net price found by deducting the discount from the list price, and the trade discount itself is never recorded in the books.
concepts.key_idea: Only the net invoice price enters the journal, so the trade discount is a calculation step and not an account.

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the list price by the discount percentage and divide by 100

solution_steps.action: deduct the discount from list price
solution_steps.explain: Subtract the trade discount from the list price to get the net invoice price

worked_examples.question_pattern: A business owns assets worth {assets} rupees and owes liabilities of {liabilities} rupees. Using the accounting equation, calculate the capital.

solution_template.explain: Deduct liabilities from total assets to obtain the capital claim

worked_examples.question_pattern: The assets of a firm are {assets} rupees and the proprietor's capital is {capital} rupees. Find the total liabilities of the firm.

solution_template.explain: Deduct capital from total assets to obtain the outsiders claim
